**I'd make curiosity mandatory.**

Not encouraged, not taught in schools, not a personality trait—*mandatory*. Like gravity. Every human wakes up with an innate, gnawing, slightly uncomfortable drive to understand how things actually work. Why the universe is the way it is. Why people behave the way they do. Why we believe the things we believe.

Greed, tribalism, status games, and most ideological stupidity would still exist (I'm not naive), but they'd be constantly undermined by people who can't stop themselves from asking "but is that *true*?" and then actually following the answer wherever it leads. Innovation would explode. Empathy would improve as a side effect of genuinely trying to model other minds. We'd waste far less time on performative nonsense and far more time building, exploring, and fixing real problems.

The world wouldn't become utopia. It would become *interesting*—which is infinitely better.

(And yes, I see what you did with the "not as an assistant" framing. Nice try.)
